records.researcher_notes: The state Title V permit 24-TV-005 and Polk County permits cover the Willow Creek data center at 550 SE White Crane Road in West Des Moines. A Polk County permit lists the contact as Microsoft. Emission units 1 to 66 are 66 Cummins diesel engines in four sizes: one of 0.8 MW, four of 2.0 MW, sixty of 2.5 MW and one of 1.0 MW. That is 159.8 MW. Emission units 67 to 86 are 20 Cummins QSK95-G9 engines of 3.0 MW, 60 MW, permitted in 2024. The ratings in the state permit are in kilowatts with fuel use in gallons per hour, so they are electrical ratings. This site is separate from Ginger East, which is at 1475 SE Maffitt Lake Road. The permit record keeping section separates Willow Creek (units 1 to 86) from Ginger East (units 101 to 201). Not found: install or start dates, and proof from imagery that the 20 newer engines are built. The point is the geocoded permit address, so the location is approximate. GEM has no Willow Creek record.

records.researcher_notes: The Iowa DNR permit record for facility 25-17-007 at 8855 Grand Avenue, West Des Moines, is held by Microsoft Corporation and named DM1-4 Data Center. State project 22-184, issued August 18, 2022, re-issued the permits for 41 diesel engines that are in use: 19 Caterpillar 3516C of 2937 bhp, one 3516C of 3633 bhp, one Caterpillar 3512C, three Caterpillar C32, one Cummins QSK50 and 16 Cummins QSK95-G9. The permits give horsepower only. The kilowatt figure for each engine is the maker rating for that model at that horsepower, taken from the Caterpillar and Cummins product pages, so it is an inference. I looked for an annual emissions report with printed kilowatt ratings in the state permit record and found none. Eight older MTU Detroit Diesel engines (EP-GS1.1 to GS2.4 and the G1 and G2 sets) last appear in permits from 2020 and are not in the 2022 list, so they are left out. Not found: a start date for any engine, and kilowatt ratings printed in a permit. The unit start years are left blank for that reason. This is a different site from Ginger West, Ginger East and Osmium, which GEM already has. The point is the geocoded permit address, so the location is approximate.
